title: Proof of a qualifying child for the Earned Income Credit
use_when: Pick this when the client must show that a child claimed for the Earned Income Credit lived with them, is related to them and meets the age test.
note: Built from IRS Form 886-H-EIC (Rev. 10-2022), which the IRS sends in EIC audits and which refers to tax year 2022; use the year being claimed. The IRS says it needs proof of all three tests, cannot accept documents signed by a relative, and needs a legal translation of documents not in English.

f886-h-eic.name: IRS, Form 886-H-EIC, Documents You Need to Send to Claim the Earned Income Credit on the Basis of a Qualifying Child or Children (Rev. 10-2022)

situations.residency: Need to show the child lived with the client for more than half the year
situations.po-box: Client uses a P.O. Box as the mailing address
situations.parent-not-on-birth-cert: Child is a son or daughter but the client's name is not on the birth certificate
situations.born-abroad: Child was not born in the United States
situations.grandchild: Child is a grandchild or great grandchild
situations.niece-nephew: Child is a niece or nephew
situations.sibling: Child is a brother, sister, half-brother or half-sister
situations.step-relative: Child is a stepchild, step-sibling, step-grandchild or step-great grandchild
situations.foster: Foster child placed by an authorized placement agency
situations.student-19-23: Child is age 19 but under 24 and a full-time student
situations.disabled: Child is permanently and totally disabled

sections.name: Residency test: the child lived with you

items.label: School records, medical records, adoption or child placement documents, or court records
items.detail: One or more. Must show your U.S. address, your name and the child's name, and dates covering more than half of the year. Medical records are from doctors, a hospital or medical clinic; the IRS notes immunization records may not include all the necessary information.

items.label: Dated statement on letterhead showing the child lived with you
items.detail: From the child's school, childcare provider (not a relative), health care provider, a social service agency, a placement agency official, your employer, an Indian tribal official, your landlord or property manager, a place of worship, or a shelter.

items.label: Another document with your name showing the same address
items.detail: Needed if a document has the child's name and your address but not your name.

items.label: Completed Form 1093, P.O. Box Application, stamped by the Post Office
Adoption records, court decree or paternity test results proving you are the parent
Birth certificate or immigration papers in English, or a legal translation
Birth certificates linking you to the grandchild
items.detail: For a grandchild: your child's and grandchild's birth certificates. For a great grandchild: your child's, grandchild's and great grandchild's. If the names are not on the birth certificates, a court decree or paternity test results.

items.label: Birth certificates or other legal documents showing how you are related to the niece or nephew
items.detail: For example the child's birth certificate showing your brother as the father, your brother's birth certificate showing your mother's name, and your own showing your mother's name. Otherwise a court decree or paternity test.

items.label: Your birth certificate and your sibling's, both naming the parent in common
items.detail: If not, another document such as a court decree or paternity test results.

items.label: Birth certificates or other legal documents, such as court papers or marriage licenses, showing the step relationship
items.detail: If the birth certificate does not name the linking parent, a court decree or DNA test results from an accredited testing laboratory listing the names of the parties involved.

items.label: Statement on letterhead from an authorized adoption agency
Statement on the letterhead of the authorized placement agency, or the court document placing the child with you during the year
School records showing the child was a full-time student for any part of five months of the tax year
items.detail: Must show the child's name and the dates the child attended school during the year. The months do not have to be consecutive.

items.label: Letter verifying the child is permanently and totally disabled
items.detail: From a doctor, other health care provider, a social service program or government agency.
